label: Weak Ricci Curvature Bounds I
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 795 through 846 and asks how a lower Ricci bound can be stated without derivatives. The answer of Lott, Sturm and Villani is to read curvature off the convexity of entropy along Wasserstein geodesics, a definition that makes sense on any metric measure space and survives geometric limits.

label: From Smooth Ricci to a Synthetic Idea
notes: On a Riemannian manifold the Bochner formula already ties a lower Ricci bound to convexity of the Boltzmann entropy along optimal transport. We promote that equivalence into a definition. Curvature becomes a statement about how mass spreads, not about the curvature tensor, which need not exist in a singular space.

label: The W2 Geodesic Stage
notes: The Wasserstein space over a geodesic metric measure space is itself geodesic. A constant speed geodesic between two measures is a displacement interpolation carried by an optimal dynamical plan. This curve is the track along which we will watch entropy, so its geometry and uniqueness questions matter for the whole construction.

label: Entropy Functionals on a Space
notes: Two functionals carry the curvature signal. The Boltzmann entropy integrates the density times its logarithm and governs the dimension free case. The Renyi style functionals integrate a power of the density and govern finite dimension N. Both are defined relative to the reference measure and are lower semicontinuous in the weak topology.

label: Distortion Coefficients
notes: Distortion coefficients measure how a unit volume of mass is stretched as it is transported a fraction of the way along a geodesic. They are built from the model space of constant curvature K over dimension N and reduce to simple sine or hyperbolic expressions. They are the precise weights that correct naive linear interpolation.

label: The CD(K,N) Definition
notes: A space satisfies the curvature dimension condition when, along every Wasserstein geodesic, the Renyi entropy obeys a convexity inequality whose interpolation weights are the distortion coefficients. This single inequality encodes a lower Ricci bound K and an upper dimension bound N simultaneously, and it requires no smooth structure to state.

label: The Convexity Inequality in Detail
notes: Reading the inequality term by term shows why it is sharp. The value of entropy at an interior time is bounded by a distortion weighted combination of the endpoint values. When curvature is positive the coefficients exceed the linear weights, forcing entropy down and concentrating mass exactly as positive Ricci should.

label: The Dimension Free Case CD(K,infinity)
notes: Letting N tend to infinity collapses the distortion coefficients to one and leaves plain K convexity of the Boltzmann entropy. This cleaner condition isolates the lower bound K alone, matches Bakry Emery theory on weighted manifolds, and is often the first synthetic bound one checks on a candidate space.

label: Examples and Sanity Checks
notes: Smooth weighted manifolds satisfy CD(K,N) exactly when their Bakry Emery Ricci tensor is bounded below by K. Euclidean space with Lebesgue measure is CD(0,N). The discrete transport laboratory in the notebook makes the corrected convexity residual visible and shows it turning negative once K is pushed too high.

label: Stability under mGH Convergence
notes: The central theorem says the curvature dimension condition is closed. If a sequence of CD(K,N) spaces converges in the measured Gromov Hausdorff sense, the limit again satisfies CD(K,N). Lower semicontinuity of entropy and convergence of optimal plans pass the inequality to the limit measure and metric.

label: Why Stability Matters
notes: Stability is what makes the synthetic definition useful rather than merely consistent. It guarantees that limits of manifolds with uniform Ricci bounds keep that bound, supplies compactness for families of such spaces, and certifies that the definition captures the right notion rather than an accident of smoothness.

label: Synthesis and Outlook
notes: We replaced the Ricci tensor by convexity of entropy along Wasserstein geodesics, weighted the inequality by distortion coefficients to encode dimension, and proved the resulting class is stable under measured Gromov Hausdorff limits. The next chapter exploits this to derive functional and geometric inequalities on the limit spaces.
